en.title: How flight attendants can be displaced from their schedule with little notice
en.summary: US flight attendants' schedules can change at short notice when flights cancel or reserves run out, but union contracts set limits and pay protection: a canceled trip can mean reassignment, reserve duty or release with the original pay kept, while the most junior crew can be forced to work a day off under a junior assignment. Outside the US, operations teams set rosters directly, usually with no extra compensation.
body: Flight attendants' schedules in the US can change at short notice in several ways, but union contracts set limits on how it happens and what they are paid when it does. When a trip or part of a trip is canceled, crew scheduling can move the affected flight attendant to another trip, put them on reserve or standby, or release them from duty entirely. Many US airline contracts call this pay protection: the crew member is paid whichever is greater, the original assignment or the new one, so a change through no fault of their own does not cut their pay. Under Alaska Airlines' 2025-2028 Collective Bargaining Agreement with the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, a line-holding flight attendant can be removed from an assignment with pay protection and flown home as a passenger, known as deadheading; reassigned or rerouted line-holders receive 150% pay, rising to 200% if the new assignment adds four or more legs over the original sequence.

Displacement is a different case: a crew member is involuntarily removed from a scheduled flight pairing or stranded away from their planned itinerary for operational needs, regulatory limits or personnel bumps, and it is not a personal absence from duty. A flight attendant can also be bumped from a trip they bid for to make room for training, new hires' supervised operating-experience flights, or a supervisor flying for qualification or observation, and then receives a similar trip or is released from duty for the rest of the trip. At Delta Air Lines, whose flight attendants are not unionised, displaced crew get no automatic pay protection and must choose between sitting on-call availability or taking a lesser payment. Frontier Airlines' 2019 contract requires at least 24 hours' notice before a flight attendant is displaced, and pays them for the trip they lost; crew scheduling typically has a window, often matching the original trip's footprint, to assign replacement flights, and if the airline does not reassign the flight attendant within those rules, the crew member is released with pay. The measure that most often catches crews off guard is the junior assignment, sometimes called junior availability: a last-resort step in which the airline forces the most junior legal flight attendant to work a flight during a scheduled day off or open time because all reserve crews have been exhausted — used in major weather disruption, holiday travel spikes or high sick-call volume, assigned from the bottom of the seniority list upward, never in violation of mandatory rest or maximum duty limits, and paid at a premium with lost days off restored. PSA Airlines' contract caps junior assignments at three days a month and bars assignments made more than 24 hours in advance, while Silver Airways' contract limited them to twice a month; both paid a 150% premium, and Alaska Airlines' 2025-2028 contract pays 2.5 times the trip rate. Silver Airways closed down in June 2025, so its terms are a historical reference.

At some airlines, flight attendants already on duty at the airport can be drafted onto another flight when time is critical or the reserve pool is empty. Reserve crews are usually more junior and on call with little notice; at American Airlines, flight attendants spend their first year on reserve, then alternate one month on and one month off until year five, when it becomes one month on and three months off under the APFA contract. At Delta, junior flight attendants have six 'A' days a month on call, keep their pay after a canceled or removed trip only if they convert to availability, and displaced lineholders are placed on availability ahead of A-Day reserves. Outside the US, airlines rarely have union agreements: rosters are set four to six weeks ahead under duty-time rules, each crew member has about three or four standby days a month in blocks of six to eight hours, and available days are filled 12 to 24 hours in advance with a trip, standby duty or a stand-down. Schedule changes simply appear on the roster, with no pay protection, sit pay or extra payments, and the terminology differs — standby instead of reserve, supernumerary flights instead of operating experience, and no junior assignment or drafting.

zh.title: 空服員班表說變就變：被調班、被迫上班與薪資保障怎麼算
zh.summary: 美國空服員的班表可能因航班取消、人力調度或最後一刻指派而改變，但工會合約設有限制與薪資保障：行程取消可改派、備勤或解除勤務並保留原薪資；最資淺者可能在休假日被強制派飛，稱為junior assignment；美國以外多由營運部門直接排班，通常沒有額外補償。
body: 美國空服員的班表可能在短時間內改變，但工會合約設有規則。航班或其中一段取消時，機組排班可將空服員改派至另一行程、轉為備勤或解除勤務；多數美國航空公司合約稱此為薪資保障，空服員可領取原定行程或新派行程較高一方的薪資，不因非自身因素的變動而減薪。阿拉斯加航空2025至2028年與空服員工會AFA-CWA的合約規定，空服員可被解除派任並以乘客身分搭機返家，即所謂deadheading；持線空服員在改派或改航時可領150%薪資，若新派行程比原行程多四段以上，薪資為200%。

被調離行程則是另一回事：空服員可能因營運需求、法規限制或人力調動，被迫離開已競標到的行程，這並非個人缺勤；也可能因訓練、新進人員帶飛或主管資格考核而被調離，此時會改派類似行程或解除當次勤務。達美航空空服員未加入工會，被調離時沒有自動薪資保障，須在待命或接受較低薪資之間選擇。邊疆航空2019年合約規定，調離前至少須24小時通知，並支付被調離行程的薪資；若未在規定時限內改派，空服員可帶薪解除勤務。最常讓人措手不及的是junior assignment：當備勤人力耗盡，航空公司可強制最資淺且符合法規的空服員在休假日或空檔執飛，常見於天氣大亂、假期高峰或大量病假；指派由該基地年資最低者依序往上，不得違反強制休息與最長工時規定，並須支付加成薪資、補回失去的休假日。PSA航空合約每月上限三天、不得提前逾24小時指派；銀色航空每月上限兩次，兩家加成薪資皆為150%，阿拉斯加航空2025至2028年合約則為2.5倍行程薪資；銀色航空已於2025年6月停業，上述條款屬歷史合約。

部分航空公司會在機場內直接徵調已在值勤的空服員改飛另一航班，稱為drafting；備勤空服員多為年資較淺者，須隨時待命。美國航空空服員第一年全程備勤，之後至第五年為一月備勤、一月不備勤，第五年起改為一月備勤、三月不備勤；達美航空空服員每月有六天A日待命，行程取消或被移除時，須轉為待命狀態才能保留薪資，達美航空的派任順序會將被調離的持線空服員優先列入待命，排在A日備勤人員之前。美國以外多無工會合約，班表由營運部門依工時法規排定，長程班表通常提前四至六週公布；每人每月約有三至四天待命，待命時段約六至八小時，可能在基地、機場或家中待命；可用日通常在12至24小時前填入行程、待命或解除勤務，班表異動不會產生薪資保障、待命津貼或額外給付；術語也不同，英國、歐洲與中東稱standby而非reserve，新進人員帶飛稱supernumerary而非operating experience，也沒有junior assignment或drafting這類制度。

facts.claim: When a trip or part of a trip is canceled, crew scheduling can move the affected flight attendant to another trip, put them on reserve/standby, or release them from duty entirely, and many US contracts pay whichever is greater: the original assignment or the new one.

Under Alaska Airlines' 2025-2028 agreement with the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA, line-holding flight attendants receive 150% pay when crew scheduling reassigns or reroutes a sequence, and 200% if assigned four or more legs over the original sequence.
Frontier Airlines' 2019 contract requires at least 24 hours' notice before a flight attendant is displaced, and pays them for the trip they lost.

A junior assignment forces the most junior legal flight attendant to work a flight during a scheduled day off or open time once all reserve crews are exhausted, and cannot violate mandatory rest requirements or maximum duty limits.

PSA Airlines' contract caps junior assignments at three days a month and bars assignments more than 24 hours in advance, while Silver Airways' contract limits them to twice a month; both paid a 150% premium, and Alaska Airlines' 2025-2028 contract pays 2.5 times the trip rate.

At American Airlines, flight attendants are on reserve for the first year, then move to one month on reserve and one month off until year five, when it becomes one month on reserve and three months off.

Outside the US, rosters are scheduled four to six weeks in advance, crew have about three or four standby days a month of six to eight hours, and schedule changes carry no pay protection, sit pay or extra payments.
